- [IARC.1.11] **One `ds_engine_t` = one independent engine.**
  An integrator may instantiate multiple `ds_engine_t`
  instances in the same process; each is fully
  independent, with its own working memory, agenda,
  rule set, clock, recorder, and Rete network. libds
  holds no global state and no singletons; every public
  function that acts on an engine takes its handle (or a
  sub-handle the engine owns) as its first argument. Four
  kinds act on none: `ds_engine_new`, which makes one; the
  `ds_json_*` functions, whose trees belong to no engine;
  `ds_free`, which releases memory libds returned; and
  `ds_build_capabilities`, which reports what the build has
  code for. All
  engine state hangs off the handle — there is no
  ambient or process-global engine context.
  Important for real-world deployments — the integration in
  particular runs multiple DS contexts (per-tier,
  per-room, per-experiment) and depends on them
  being independent within one process. Combined
  with [IARC.1.10], it means an integrator can pump
  N engines from one async runtime without any
  threading or cross-engine interference.

  Test obligations: `spec/test_arch_invariants_spec`
  pins the per-engine isolation invariant black-box
  (facts, clock state, stream callbacks, typed
  callbacks, and rule sets are all per-engine; no
  cross-engine bleed). The schema-registry slice of
  the same invariant lives in
  `spec/test_schema_registry_spec` per IDAT.5.5.
